how_presence_WAS_established: Two send-message calls each returned rc=0 with a MessageId, and get-queue-attributes then read ApproximateNumberOfMessages=2.
A_METHOD_CORRECTION_THAT_MATTERS_AT_GRAD: An SQS receive-message is a SAMPLE, not a census: it polls a subset of servers, so it can omit a message that is present. Measured here -- a receive with max-number-of-messages 10 and 15s long polling returned only the SCHWAB record while the depth read 2 and both sends were acked. Earlier, in the OG-ap-11 grade, the same call returned the SAME eclipse message ten times. So: a receive that RETURNS a message proves PRESENCE; a receive that OMITS one proves NOTHING about absence. This corrects a claim I made during the ap-11 grade, that 'the receive is authoritative and the counter lags' -- neither is a census. ap-11's verdict is unaffected (it FAILED on the report half, and its depth independently fell 2 -> 1), but the stated basis for 'schwab was drained' was an absence inferred from a sample, which is not sound. At THIS grade, absence is read from the depth falling plus the sweep's own report, never from a message failing to appear in one receive.
